intro: The Safety Framework sets out the integrated system of principles, practices, and responsibilities that guide how safety is planned, managed, and continuously improved across all sport activities and operations.

pillars.name: Commitment
pillars.body: Leadership commitment is the foundation of effective safety management. It means that those at the top of the organisation — boards, executives, and managers — visibly champion safety, allocate adequate resources, and hold themselves accountable for outcomes.
elements: Safety as a standing agenda item

pillars.name: Culture
pillars.body: A strong safety culture exists when every individual — staff, coaches, contractors, and volunteers — internalises safety as a shared value rather than a compliance obligation. Culture is built through consistent leadership behaviour, open reporting, and learning from incidents.

pillars.name: Competencies
pillars.body: Safe sport delivery depends on people having the knowledge, skills, and judgement to identify hazards, apply controls, and respond to emergencies. Competency is built through structured training, credentialing, and regular refreshers.
elements: Mandatory certifications for coaches and instructors

pillars.name: Controls
pillars.body: Controls are the physical, procedural, and administrative measures that reduce the likelihood and severity of harm. Effective control means applying the hierarchy — eliminate the hazard first, then substitute, engineer, administrate, and lastly use PPE.

pillars.name: Collaboration
pillars.body: No single person or team owns safety. Collaboration means partners, contractors, national sport associations, and facility operators work together through shared standards, joint planning, and mutual accountability.

pillars.name: Communication
pillars.body: Safety information must reach the right people at the right time. This covers everything from pre-event safety briefings and signage to ongoing reporting of hazards, near-misses, and incidents — and the feedback loop that closes the loop on action taken.

domains.name: Leadership & Governance
domains.body: The board and executive layer sets safety direction, approves policy, and monitors performance through defined governance structures and reporting lines.

domains.name: Policy & Strategy
domains.body: Policies translate governance intent into binding requirements. Strategy sets the multi-year direction for safety improvement aligned to Vision 2030.

domains.name: Innovation & Technology
domains.body: Technology and data are leveraged to improve hazard detection, incident reporting, training delivery, and safety performance monitoring.

domains.name: Competence & Capability
domains.body: Building the human capital needed to deliver safe sport — through training pipelines, credentialing schemes, and succession planning for safety-critical roles.

domains.name: Stakeholder Expectations
domains.body: Understanding and responding to the safety expectations of athletes, participants, partners, regulators, and the public.

domains.name: Risk Management
domains.body: Systematic identification, assessment, treatment, and monitoring of risks across all sport programmes, events, and facilities.

domains.name: Planning & Assurance
domains.body: Operational safety plans, audit programmes, and assurance reviews that verify controls are in place and effective.

domains.name: Performance & Improvement
domains.body: Tracking safety KPIs, learning from incidents, and driving continuous improvement across the organisation.

domains.name: Information & Intelligence
domains.body: Collecting and analysing safety data — incidents, near-misses, audits, and benchmarks — to generate actionable insights.

domains.name: Regulatory Obligations
domains.body: Compliance with the Workplace Safety and Health Act, sport-specific statutory requirements, and applicable codes of practice.

domains.name: Operational Management
domains.body: Day-to-day safety management of facilities, programmes, and events — the operational layer where policy is put into practice.

domains.name: Duty of Care
domains.body: The legal and ethical responsibility shared by all who deliver or host sport to take reasonable steps to prevent foreseeable harm.
